搓衣板的音色具有明亮、清脆的質感，帶有獨特的金屬質地。其高頻成分突出，音域集中在: The washboard has a bright, crisp timbre with a distinctive metallic quality. Its high frequencies stand out and its range sits in the upper middle, so it cuts through the other parts of a band. Striking the ridged metal surface produces a continuous sandy rasp and the clatter of metal on metal, giving rich overtones; scraping gives a warm, coarse, rubbed texture instead. It resonates in its own way: the wooden frame provides a moderate body while the metal ribs sound directly, which places its character between percussion and metal instruments. Compared with the bright sharpness of cymbals, the washboard is gentler; compared with the warmth of a xylophone, it is harder and coarser. The traps fitted to it, such as cowbells and woodblocks, add layers to the tone and a raw folk-music flavour.
洗衣板作為打擊樂器源自西非 hamboning（一種節奏實踐），經被奴役非洲人傳: The washboard as a percussion instrument comes from West African hamboning, a rhythmic practice, and reached the Americas with enslaved Africans, leading in the 1920s to jug bands that kept time with a jug, spoons and a washboard; well-known players include Washboard Doc, Washboard Willie and Washboard Sam. Its variant the frottoir is an American instrument invented in the mid-twentieth century for zydeco, designed in 1946 by Clifton Chenier and made by Willie Landry: the wooden frame was dropped and the corrugated metal face kept, with a shoulder strap. In 2010 the electric washboard, the Woogie Board, appeared.
洗衣板可保留木框，持法有三種：垂直垂於胸前、水平橫於膝上，或夾於腿間以便兩面同時: A washboard may keep its wooden frame, and it can be held in three ways: hanging vertically on the chest, lying horizontally across the knees, or gripped between the legs so that both faces can be played. It sounds mainly by being struck, though the corrugated face can also be scraped with thimbles; in a jug band a whisk or a wire drum brush strokes it, and most tunes hit only the backbeat, taking the place of the snare drum. Begin in four-beat units, stroking steadily on beats 2 and 4, then practise the thimble work used in jazz. The zydeco board has no frame and hangs from the neck; the player holds a spoon handle or a bottle opener in each hand and strokes, scrapes, strikes and rolls, up to eight to sixteen strokes in a four-beat bar, in a rhythm closer to the Latin güiro.

The other, frameless type hangs only a corrugated metal plate from the neck and is played with a spoon handle or a bottle opener, whose materials the source likewise does not give.
洗衣板樂器屬體鳴，見於美洲／北美，在傳統爵士、齊德科、斯基菲、水罐樂團與老式音樂: The washboard is an idiophone, found in North America and appearing in traditional jazz, zydeco, skiffle, jug bands and old-time music. Jug bands often stroke it with a single wire brush or a whisk on beats 2 and 4, taking the place of the snare drum; in jazz, thimbles can beat out complex rhythms. The frottoir in a zydeco band is usually hung from the neck and stroked with a bottle opener or a spoon handle, playing cross-rhythms against the drummer in a rhythm close to the güiro. It is also used occasionally at Polish traditional jazz festivals and in Ukrainian folk music, and it appears in blues, punk rock, rhythm and blues, folk punk, Southern rock, hill-country blues and New Orleans traditional jazz line-ups.

The washboard and the zydeco frottoir are idiophone percussion instruments, Hornbostel–Sachs number 112.25, found in North America. The washboard keeps its wooden frame and corrugated metal face, is played by striking and by scraping with thimbles, and may be fitted with a wooden fish and cowbells; the frottoir has no frame, its corrugated metal face hangs from the neck, and it is scraped, struck and rolled with a spoon handle or a bottle opener. Both are used in jazz, zydeco, skiffle, jug bands and old-time music; the washboard usually replaces the drum, while the frottoir is often played alongside the drummer; Polish traditional jazz festivals and Ukrainian folk music use them occasionally as well.
